name: Garden Egg Fruit Rot
scientificName: Phytophthora spp., Fusarium spp., Phomopsis vexans
description: A complex of fungal diseases causing rotting of garden egg fruits both in the field and after harvest. The fruit becomes soft, water-soaked, and covered with fungal growth. Losses can be severe during wet weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on fruits that enlarge rapidly
Fruits developing soft, sunken rotten areas
White or grey fungal growth on rotting fruit
Fruits dropping prematurely from the plant
Dark lesions on fruit stems spreading to fruit
Rot continuing in stored fruits after harvest
causes: Fungal spores splashed onto fruits by rain
Poor air circulation in dense plantings
treatments: Remove and destroy infected fruits immediately
Apply copper-based fungicide spray to fruits and foliage
Spray mancozeb or metalaxyl at first sign of infection
Improve air circulation by pruning excess foliage
prevention: Avoid harvesting during or immediately after rain
Keep fruits off soil surface using mulch or stakes
Ensure good air circulation through proper spacing
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
Store harvested fruits in cool, dry, well-ventilated area
